solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Taken medium English vegetable boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the vegetable holds the next two letters within it

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable
M is the standard abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone collects a medium-sized box of English vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' looks like a verb about the boxes, but it is the definition in its sense of captivated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken with someone is to be delighted or enchanted by them, a synonym of being charmed.

clue.text: Dessert stain's beginning to disappear from dress

indicators.note: to disappear from means the letter is taken away from the dressing word

parts.note: compost is used to dress soil, a top dressing for gardens

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dessert stain begins to fade from a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like clothing; here it is the gardening sense of a soil dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A compote of fruit stewed in syrup is served as a pudding or sweet course.

clue.text: Insecure lady shunning outside with separation

indicators.note: shunning the outside means dropping the first and last letters of lady

parts.note: a rift is a split or separation

explanation.surface: An anxious woman avoids going outdoors after a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoored, drifting, without anchor: loose and not secured in place.

clue.text: Satisfied in peace, lifted beer bottle

parts.note: to meet a requirement is to satisfy it

indicators.note: in means the reversed beer goes inside the word for peace

parts.note: hush means peace and quiet

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: Contented, in peace, someone raises a bottle of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beer bottle' reads as one item; only 'bottle' is the definition and 'beer' gives ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine or champagne container holding eight standard measures, named after the long-lived patriarch.

clue.text: Cheat, only to have university raising question

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the university letter moves it upwards, earlier in the word

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child

explanation.surface: A cheat at university has his work called into question.
explanation.definitionFit: To question something is to call it into doubt, a verb meaning suspect.

clue.text: Newly target officials restricting old copper

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the officials surround the next letters

parts.note: refs is short for referees, sports officials
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police force sets new targets while its bosses keep an old-fashioned bobby in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim attention again at a fresh goal is a verb sense matching to target anew.

clue.text: Teller against cutting fee, you are told

indicators.note: cutting means piercing, so the word for against goes into the fee

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: told means spoken, so these words give letters that sound like them

parts.note: the letters U R sound like you are, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A bank teller objects to a reduced fee, so you are informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teller' suggests a bank clerk; the answer tells tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled storyteller who entertains with anecdotes is someone who tells.

clue.text: President, one of the predecessors to Roosevelt?

parts.words: one of the predecessors to Roosevelt?
parts.note: Franklin Roosevelt is known by his three initials, and the two letters ahead of his R are the predecessors; one of the two is offered as a choice

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking which earlier US president came before Roosevelt.
explanation.walkthrough: In FDR the letters before R are F and D, so 'one of' them is F OR D. Gerald Ford in fact came long after Roosevelt; the question mark flags the letter play.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th US head of state, so an example of a president.

clue.text: Erratic working to circumvent current standards

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go around, so the anagram encloses the letter for current
working means in operation, here worked into a new letter order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Erratic work dodges current standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles or benchmarks by which things are judged are the standards measured against.

clue.text: Strippers use these very large gatherings to go topless

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top letter, the first in a down entry

parts.note: events are gatherings or occasions

explanation.surface: Strip clubs hold very big parties where people go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strippers' suggests striptease; here it means paint strippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint and varnish strippers are chemical liquids that dissolve coatings.

clue.text: Value characters coming back from retirement

indicators.note: coming back means the run of letters is read in the reverse direction
characters are letters, here a run of letters lifted out of the next word
from tells us which word supplies the run of letters

explanation.surface: Something worthwhile is found in the people returning from retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth or excellence, the value of something, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A French drink is not pleasant

definitions.note: the definition with its link verb: the answer describes what is not pleasant

parts.note: un is the French for a or one
a cordial is a sweet drink, often a fruit concentrate

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a particular French drink tastes unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' as a drink is a British fruit squash concentrate; the answer is its negative adjective, unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking warmth or friendliness, the opposite of genial, matches being not pleasant.

clue.text: Future surrounding play on golf course is dispiriting

indicators.note: surrounding means the future word wraps around the golf term

parts.note: in the offing means coming soon, so the offing is the near future
to putt is to play the ball on the green of a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer gloomily foresees poor play on the course ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting or discouraging puts you off, which is what dispiriting describes.

clue.text: Add wrapping around this present, that will be stuck

indicators.note: around this says the outside pair of letters from the first word sit beside this answer, so taking them away recovers it

parts.note: a thing that will be stuck is one that will stick, a verb meaning cling

indicators.note: the wrapping of a word is its outside letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Gift-wrapping instructions: add paper around this present and tape will hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive clue: the clue describes the answer as what is left of a word for stick once the wrapping of 'Add' is put around it and taken away again; 'present' here means in attendance, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Present in the sense of being in attendance, as in a roll call reply, means in this place.

clue.text: Rodent put in fridge breaks porcelain

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the chilling word goes into the porcelain

parts.note: china is fine porcelain
to chill something is to cool it in the fridge

explanation.surface: A rodent put in the fridge breaks the china.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American animal bred for its soft fur, a member of the rodent order.

clue.text: Phrase used on first dates?

parts.note: a romantic first date is the surface, but the earliest dates in the calendar are those before year one, written BC

explanation.surface: A question about a line to try on a romantic first date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First dates' suggests courting; the answer is the phrase behind BC, used for the earliest years in history.
explanation.definitionFit: The era abbreviation BC labels the oldest calendar years, the earliest dates there are.

clue.text: Person shrewd, collecting our rent in oppressive manner

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the person and shrewd words hold the shuffled letters

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should
sly means cunning or shrewd

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrewd landlord collects our rent in an oppressive way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money for a landlord; it is the past of rend, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdensomely or heavily, in a way that weighs on people, is an adverb of oppression.

clue.text: Enigmatic stranger losing temper with bully around

indicators.note: around means the word for bully wraps around the shortened stranger

parts.note: to abuse is to mistreat or bully

indicators.note: losing means taking away the letters of temper from stranger

parts.note: anger is temper or rage

explanation.surface: An enigmatic stranger keeps his temper while a bully hangs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ANGER out of STRANGER, leaving STR.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure and hard to understand, like a mystery, is the sense of puzzling.

clue.text: Resident's fall eating baked product

indicators.note: eating means the fall word takes the baked item inside

parts.note: to occur is to fall, as a date falls on a Monday
a pie is a baked product

explanation.surface: A resident tumbles while eating a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests a tumble; it means happen, as a holiday falls on a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in or holding a property is its inhabitant, a resident.

clue.text: Acting like bootlegger, announced dollar per piece of jewellery

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, per gives an, and an earring is a piece of jewellery: a buck an earring

explanation.surface: A smuggler's price list announced at a dollar for each piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Per' gives AN, as in a pound an hour; BUCK AN EARRING spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleggers smuggle illicit goods, and acting like a pirate or freebooting adventurer fits that lawless trade.

clue.text: Protein-rich food, case of prize fish turned up

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last
in a down entry, turned up means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A prize fish is turned up as a source of protein.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume eaten as a nut, packed with protein, is a protein-rich food.

clue.text: Is learner driver also in pedestrian area?

parts.note: L is the plate shown by a learner driver
and means also

explanation.surface: A question whether a learner driver has strayed into a pedestrianised zone.
explanation.walkthrough: A traffic island is a raised refuge in the middle of a road where pedestrians wait to cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic refuge where walkers stand safely mid-road is an area for pedestrians.

clue.text: Rough stray caught scratching around

indicators.note: to stray is to wander, so the remaining letters wander into a new order
scratching means striking out, removing letters from the word caught

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or approximately

explanation.surface: A rough-looking stray cat is caught scratching around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' strikes CA from CAUGHT, leaving UGHT, which 'stray' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a noun for a violent hooligan, the same as a ruffian or brute.

clue.text: Canteen carrying on keeping meal cool

indicators.note: carrying means the canteen holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: a mess is a military canteen or dining hall

indicators.note: keeping means the little word holds the meal within it

parts.note: a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: A canteen carries on keeping a meal chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool as a noun means fashionable style, and being in vogue is the quality the answer names.

clue.text: One unoccupied snug oddly ignored by indulgers

indicators.note: ignored by means these letters are left out of the word indulgers

parts.note: the letters of snug taken in an odd, jumbled order, N U G S, as they appear in indulgers

explanation.surface: Someone at a loose end in a snug pub is pointedly ignored by the drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like alternate letters, but it scrambles SNUG, whose letters N, U, G, S are then removed from INDULGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with nothing to do, lazing around, is a person not occupied with work.

clue.text: College tutor lacking heart

indicators.note: lacking heart means the central letter of the tutoring word is dropped

parts.note: to tutor is to teach

explanation.surface: A college tutor is described as lacking compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: A tech is British slang for a technical college.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form for a technical college or polytechnic, an institution of further education.

clue.text: Cutting vessel, jugular vein's fluid all over the place

indicators.note: fluid means shifting and not fixed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
cutting means removing, so the vessel's letters are cut out of the fodder

parts.note: a jug is a vessel for pouring

explanation.surface: A grisly picture of a blood vessel in the neck cut open, its fluid everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' removes JUG from JUGULARVEINS; 'fluid' rearranges ULARVEINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Found everywhere, applying in every case, is the sense of being widespread across the place.

clue.text: Cockney got love from East End girl

indicators.note: reading from the east end of an across entry means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: had with the h dropped, as a Cockney speaker would say it
love is zero in tennis, so nil

explanation.surface: A Cockney man won the love of a girl from the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, traditionally drop the H, so had becomes 'AD. 'East End' looks like the Cockney home; it says read from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: See about painting hospital being feasible

indicators.note: about means going round, so the see wraps around the next letters

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city and see in Cambridgeshire
art covers painting
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a painting for the hospital is a possibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb but a bishop's seat, the usual crossword use of ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: As in no earthly chance, the adjective means conceivable or possible at all.

clue.text: Criticised good person close to me in a way

indicators.note: in means the saint and letter go inside the word for a way

parts.note: a road is a way, a route to travel
ST, short for saint, is the crossword good person

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A good person near the speaker gets criticised in a way.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them severely, so a past form meaning slated.
